classification.difficultyReason: Requires proving both directions using triangle congruence.

content.prompt: Prove that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle if and only if $\angle A=\angle B=\angle C$. Hint: An equilateral triangle is an isosceles triangle.

answer.short:
Equal angles give equal opposite sides, so the triangle is equilateral. Conversely, equal sides give equal opposite angles.

Apply AAS and RHS to pairs of triangles formed by altitudes to prove these equalities.
answer.worked:
Suppose $\angle A=\angle B=\angle C$. Draw the altitude $AD$ to $BC$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABD&=\angle ACD &&\text{(given)}\\\angle ADB&=\angle ADC=90^\circ &&\text{(altitude)}\\AD&=AD &&\text{(shared side)}\end{align*}$$
Thus $\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ACD$ by AAS, so $AB=AC$. Similarly, draw the altitude from $B$ to $AC$. The resulting right triangles are congruent by AAS because $\angle A=\angle C$ and the altitude is shared. Hence $AB=BC$. Therefore $AB=BC=CA$, so $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.

Conversely, suppose $AB=BC=CA$. Draw the altitude $AD$ to $BC$.
$$\begin{align*}AB&=AC &&\text{(equilateral triangle)}\\AD&=AD &&\text{(shared side)}\\\angle ADB&=\angle ADC=90^\circ &&\text{(altitude)}\end{align*}$$
Thus $\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ACD$ by RHS, so $\angle B=\angle C$. Similarly, an altitude from $C$ gives right triangles congruent by RHS, so $\angle A=\angle B$. Therefore $\angle A=\angle B=\angle C$.
